summary: Postel assigns ranges of host-host protocol link numbers for the Message Switching Protocol experiment, for network measurement under the UCLA Network Measurement Center, and for private experiments, and corrects the link assignment table. It was replaced by RFC 604.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 317 assigns link-number ranges for network measurement and a Message Switching Protocol experiment. It also republishes the corrected Host-Host link assignment table.

questions: what were the arpanet link number assignments
which links were assigned for measurement
subtitle: A 1972 update assigns Host-Host link numbers for measurement and an experiment.

tldr.problem: The Host-Host Protocol's link assignment table needed specific ranges for network measurement and the Message Switching Protocol experiment.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 317 assigns links 192 through 195 to the Message Switching Protocol experiment and links 159 through 190 for measurement under the Network Measurement Center.
tldr.outcome: It also corrects the link assignment table in NIC 8246. The RFC was later obsoleted by RFC 604.

today: RFC 317 is historic and was obsoleted by RFC 604. It records link-number assignments and a correction to the Host-Host Protocol assignment table.

sections.title: Additional Link Assignments
sections.content: RFC 317 assigns Host-Host Protocol links 192, 193, 194, and 195 to the Message Switching Protocol experiment. It assigns links 159 through 190 for network measurement under the direction of the Network Measurement Center.
sections.plainLanguage: Some link numbers are set aside for particular work. This RFC assigns a range to measurement and four links to an experiment.

sections.title: The Corrected Assignment Table
sections.content: The corrected table lists link 0 as the Control Link; 2 through 71 as available for connections; 1 and 72 through 158 as reserved; 159 through 191 for measurement under the UCLA Network Measurement Center; 192 through 195 for the Message Switching Protocol experiment; and 196 through 255 for private experimental use.
sections.plainLanguage: The table separates the link numbers into control, connection, reserved, measurement, and experimental uses. It gives each range and its assignment.

sections.title: Correction and Later Status
sections.content: RFC 317 says that the link assignment table on page 28 of NIC 8246 should read as reproduced in the document. The unit metadata lists RFC 604 as the RFC that later obsoleted RFC 317.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC corrects the earlier table so readers have a consistent assignment list. A later RFC replaced this document.
